set.st: Michael Tweit, a recluse farmer and son of Thor Tweit (in Blue Earth Co. by about 1871, a well-off family), died 12 Jun 1927. His obituary says "it is generally rumored that he had buried money and hid it otherwise about his farm." He had once been committed to the St. Peter asylum, the obituary says 'railroaded' by people after his money; the Farmers' National Bank of Waseca administered the estate and held an administrator's sale on 21 June 1927. No recovery was reported 1927-32. Pin is the Twite farmstead in the SE¼ sec 14 (1914 atlas, 1938 aerial), not a spot. In 1906 he inherited a third of his mother's real estate in Medo Twp., Blue Earth Co.
pinev: 1938 aerial farmstead (MHAPO we05224) on the Twite SE¼ sec 14 T105N R24W, the tract Mamie Hanson held in 1937; r 120 m
1914 Webb atlas places the Tweit land in the SE¼ sec 14
1920 census: a Michael Tweit b. 1867 Iowa enumerated in St. Peter Ward 2 (the state hospital, which fits the obituary's asylum stay). Not in the 1914 Waseca plat patron list.

1927 administrator's auction ad: sale 'on the Tweit farm 3 miles south and 3 miles east of Waldorf and 8 miles west of New Richland on the County Gravel Road No. 6'. The bearings meet about 43.891,-93.640 (Byron Twp), about 2 mi E of the sec 14 tract; road miles, or a second parcel. Pin stays on the platted farmstead pending a check.
1914 Waseca farmer directories list no Tweit under Waldorf or New Richland; the auction bearing falls in sec 19 T105N R23W (Byron Twp).
